scope: Two vendored memory modules read whole/pin verified/syntax parsed. Neither imported: process module performs runtime probes at import; no probes/GC capture executed.
findings: Process fallback explicitly returns zero metrics when unavailable; availability must accompany numbers to distinguish unsupported from zero memory. resource fallback measures peakRSS while ps/proc measure currentRSS, so values are not temporally interchangeable.

Linux proc parser whitespace-splits entire stat record, although parenthesized comm may contain spaces; fixed field indices can shift. os_specific appends on each update without clearing, duplicating retained status entries. Static findings.
ps collector has no timeout and trusts last two tokens if at least two exist; malformed/header-only output can raise numeric conversion error.
ObjectTracker deliberately retains strong references to all captured objects, preventing their collection. Apparent retention under this tool is not neutral evidence of application leak.
Tracker ignore_self relies on exact gc.get_referrers counts, and object capture is not atomic across active threads. Caller-supplied ignore lists are mutated and cleared.
SummaryTracker.diff advances baseline even when explicit summary1 provided and summary2 absent; consumers need documented lifecycle when comparing multiple phases.
